references.text: Describes how Israel completely destroyed Jericho and everything in the city, which is the preceding event referred to in Joshua 8:2.
Tells of the destruction of Jericho by fire, which parallels what was to happen at Ai.
The law concerning war spoils that allowed the Israelites to take cattle and goods as plunder, something permitted at Ai but not at Jericho.
The fulfillment of the promise that Israel could take the spoil and livestock from Ai for themselves.
Describes the execution of the ambush that God commanded in verse 2.
A similar military strategy involving an ambush was used against Gibeah, which recalls the tactics employed against Ai.
Refers back to the destruction of both Jericho and Ai and their kings.
